Republic of the Philippines DEPARTML OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, QUEZON Www.dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT BIVAHENG PINOY TAPA NA PALAXAD. UAm.AD 22 APR 2014 DILG Legal opinion No. 12, S. 2014 HON. RANDY RUEL D. BEGTANG Vice-Mayor Conner, Apayao Dear Vice-Mayor Begtang: This has reference to letter asking the Department's opinion and guidance on whether Mr. Artemio Gonayon, a losing candidate for the position of Sangguniang Bayan Member last 2013 Synchronized Local and Barangay Elections, is qualified to represent the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) of Conner, Apayao and if answered in the affirmative, whether he will sit as member of the Sangguniang Bayan with the same privileges and wages as the other regular SB members. Per your letter, Mr. Artemio Gonayon ran as Sangguniang Bayan Member last 2013 Synchronized Local and Barangay Elections but lost. Immediately thereafter, he was selected to represent the ICCs/IPs of Conner Apayao in accordance with the local guideline adopted and promulgated by the said ICCs/IPs. According to you, you are familiar with Section 4, Rule XIII of the Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, series of 1998, as amended), which provides as follows: "Section 4 A person who lost in an election (except Barangay Election) shall not be eligible for appointment or reemployment to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporation within one year following such election. " Thus, your subject letter-request. Your queries may be re-stated as follows: 1. Is Mr. Ganayon qualified to represent the ICCs,4Ps of Conner, Apayao? 2. If answered in the affirmative, can he sit as member of the Sangguniang Bayan with the same compensation and benefits as the other regular SB members? As to the first issue, Mr. Ganayon is qualified to represent the ICCs/IPs if he met all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications set forth in the Local Guideline adopted and promulgated by the ICCs/IPs themselves regarding the selection of a particular ICC/IP representative.

With regard to the second issue on whether Mr. Ganayon can sit as member of the Sangguniang Bayan of Conner, Apayao given the prohibition under Section 4, Rule XIII of the Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, series of 1998, as amended), we deem it proper to first discuss certain principles. Well-settled is the rule that a person acquires public office either by appointment or by election. An appointment is the act or designation by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given officel. On the other hand, an election "means the choice or selection of candidates to public office by popular vote through the use of the ballot, and the elected officials are determined through the will of the electorate'"2. An election is the embodiment of the popular will, the expression Of the sovereign power of the people. The 1987 Constitution prohibits the appointment of a losing candidate, within one after such election, to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of its subsidiaries, thus: Section 6, Article IX-B, 1987 Constitution "No candidate who has lost in any election, shall within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of its subsidiaries. " The foregoing Constitutional provision is reiterated under Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 and pertinent CSC issuances, thus: Section 94, Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991) "SECTION 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidate Who Lost in an Election.—xxx (b) Except for losing candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the Government or any government- owned or-controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries. " Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and OtherPersonneI Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended) "Section 4. A person who lost in an election (excep t Barangay election) shall not be eligible for appointment or reemployment to any I Mechem, Section 102. 2 Rulloda vs. COMELEC, G.R. No. 154198, 20 January 2003).

ofFce in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporation within one year following such election. " The rationale behind this prohibition is the extirpation of the "spoils system," considering that the foregoing provisions are directed against the so-called "political lameducks'%'. Then came Republic Act No. 8371 or the Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997, which was approved and signed into law on 29 October 1997. Said law provides that the Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) have the right to participate fully, if they so choose, at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them as well as to maintain and develop their own indigenous political structures. Said law recognizes the policy of the State in affording the indigenous people communities adequate representations in the local sanggunians at a//levels. On 28 October 2009, the NCIP issued NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 2009 prescribing national guidelines for the mandatory representation of indigenous peoples in the local sanggunians. Section 12 thereof provides and we quote: "SECTION 12. Selection and Assumption to Office. The selection of the particular ICC/IP representative to the local legislative council shall be in accordance with the Local Guideline that the concerned ICCs/IPs shall adopt and promulgate, which considers the cycle of traditional or local activities, and must be compliant to this Administrative Order by containing, at least, the following: a. b. c. d. e. g. h. i. j. Title; Definitions of Terms; Selection precess which should make a delineation of representation to the levels of Barangay, Municipality, City and Province; Qualifications and Disqualifications; Community Confirmation and Nomination; Vacancy; Disciplinary A ction; Term of Office; Recall/Remova1; Special Provisions, if any; Amendment; and Effectivity Clause. For the purpose of ensuring uniformity in the form of the Local Guidelines to be adopted by the concerned ICCs/IPs, the Office of Empowerment and Human Rights (OEHR) shall develop and make available a guide form. 3 CSC Resolution No. 02-0012, Gato, Vicente S.

Assumption to Office shall take place as soon as the is formally certified by the concerned NCIP Regional Director, upon recommendation of the Provincial or Community Service Center head, as the case may be, to be in accordance with this Administrative Order, and the person chosen takes the appropriate oath before authorized officer and informs the appropriate body/ies of his/her assumption. (Emphasis Supplied) As could be gleaned from the foregoing, RA 8371 and NCIP Administrative Order No. 001, series of 2009 used another term, that is, selection vis-å-vis the representative of ICCs/IPs in the local sanggunians. The next issue therefore is how we would categorize "selection", the mode in which the ICC/IP representative is chosen, is it within the term "election" so that the ICC/IP representative shall be considered as an elective official, or within the term "appointment" so that the IP/ICC representative is an appointed official, thus within the proscription under Section 6, Article IX-B of the 1987 Constitution as reiterated under Section 94 of RA 7160 and Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended)? The Department is of the view that the position of ICCJIP representative is necessarily elective in nature, thus, notwithin the prohibition under the Constitution, RA 7160 and CSC issuance for the following reasons: 1. As already defined above, an appointment is the act or designation by the executive officer, board or body to where that power has been delegated, of the individual who is to exercise the functions of a given office. May it be respectfully noted that it is not the NCIP or this Department which selects the ICC/IP representative. Under the aforequoted Section 12 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009, the ICCs/IPs themselves chose the particular ICC/IP representative to the local sanggunian in accordance with their Local Guideline that they themselves have adopted or promulgated for the purpose. The only participation of the NCIP in the process is the issuance, thru their Regional Office, of a Certificate of Affirmation (COA) to the chosen ICC/IP representative and on the basis of such confirmation, this Department shall thereafter accord due recognition to him/her4. 2. This Department has been consistent in its opinion that it is not the mode to which one acquired office that determines the nature and character of such office. It is the function or role of said office that is controlling. Our classic example is the case of two (2) incumbent regular sanggunian members who were appointed therein to fill the permanent vacancies in the aforesaid August Body. While it may be true that they acquired their positions thru appointment, they should not be considered as appointive members of the sanggunian. The nature and character of the office of the regular member of the Section 16, NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009.

sanggunian is elective, the assumption to which, while generally determined by an election, is not precluded by appointment to fill the permanent vacancies that may arise therein. RA 8371 mandates the representation of ICCs/IPs in the local sanggunians at all levels. Such IP/ICC representative shall represent the ICCs/IPs at all levels of decision-making in matters which may affect their rights, lives and destinies through procedures determined by them and in doing so, the ICC/IP representative necessarily will propose in the local sanggunian legislative measures (i.e. ordinance/resolution) towards developing ICC/IP conditions and participate in the deliberations thereof. In fact, in DILG Opinion No. 20, series of 2011, the ICC/IP representative was referred as "ex-officio member of the local sanggunian", the same term that we use to refer to the president of the liga ng mga barangay and sangguniang kabataan from municipal to provincial levels; 3. Lastly, Section 6, Rule IV of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 8371 as reiterated under Section 13 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009, categorically states that the ICC/IP representative shall have the same compensation. benefits and other emoluments as the regular members of the legislative bodies and/or policy making bodies. Based on the foregoing and in reply to your query, we are of the view the position of ICC/IP representative is necessarily elective in nature thus, not within the purview of the aforequoted prohibition under the 1987 Constitution, RA 7160 and CSC issuance. Accordingly, therefore, Mr. Ganayon can sit as ICC/IP representative in the Sangguniang Bayan of Conner, Apayao and shall have the same compensation, benefits and other emoluments as the regular members of the aforesaid August Body, provided however that a COA has been issued by the concerned NCIP Field Office to his favor and that he was duly recognized by the Department pursuant to Section 16 of NCIP AO No. 001, series of 2009. On a final note, the foregoing opinion however does not preclude you or other concerned party/ies from seeking a more authoritative opinion from the Department of Justice since the issue posed involves a legal issue. The foregoing initial opinion was rendered since you cited a similar provision of the Local Government Code of 1991, the law which this Department is primarily tasked to interpret. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Ve ly yours, AUSTERE A. PAN ERO Undersecretary L.s/17 Comu rn ished: RD JOHN M. CASTANEDA DILG-CAR Barangay Center, Upper Session Road Baguio City
